Design a 2-channel DMA (Direct Memory Access) controller in Verilog. The controller should have two channels, each capable of transferring data independently. Each channel should have a request (req) and acknowledge (ack) signal. The DMA controller should prioritize channel 1 over channel 2. When both channels have a request, channel 1 should be served first. The controller should also have a busy signal indicating whether it is currently transferring data.
code:
module dma_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input req1,      // Channel 1 request
    input req2,      // Channel 2 request
    output reg ack1, // Channel 1 acknowledge
    output reg ack2, // Channel 2 acknowledge
    output reg busy  // Busy signal
);

    reg [1:0] state; // 00: Idle, 01: Transfer Channel 1, 10: Transfer Channel 2

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Idle state
            ack1 <= 0;
            ack2 <= 0;
            busy <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin // Idle
                    if (req1) begin
                        state <= 2'b01; // Go to Transfer Channel 1
                        busy <= 1;
                    end else if (req2) begin
                        state <= 2'b10; // Go to Transfer Channel 2
                        busy <= 1;
                    end
                end
                2'b01: begin // Transfer Channel 1
                    ack1 <= 1; // Acknowledge Channel 1
                    if (!req1) begin
                        ack1 <= 0; // No longer acknowledging Channel 1
                        busy <= 0;
                        state <= 2'b00; // Back to Idle
                    end
                end
                2'b10: begin // Transfer Channel 2
                    ack2 <= 1; // Acknowledge Channel 2
                    if (!req2) begin
                        ack2 <= 0; // No longer acknowledging Channel 2
                        busy <= 0;
                        state <= 2'b00; // Back to Idle
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

The module should keep track of the current window size, the next packet to send, and acknowledge received packets. The sender should have a state machine to handle sending packets based on the window size and the acknowledgment received.
code:
module sliding_window_protocol #(parameter WINDOW_SIZE = 4, parameter PACKET_SIZE = 8) (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input send_packet,
    input ack,
    output reg [PACKET_SIZE-1:0] packet_out,
    output reg valid_out
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 00: IDLE, 01: SENDING, 10: WAITING_ACK
    reg [3:0] sent_count; // Number of packets sent

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= 0;
            sent_count <= 0;
            packet_out <= 0;
            valid_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // IDLE
                    valid_out <= 0;
                    if (send_packet && sent_count < WINDOW_SIZE) begin
                        packet_out <= sent_count; // Sending packet with count
                        valid_out <= 1;
                        sent_count <= sent_count + 1;
                        state <= 1; // Move to SENDING state
                    end
                end
                1: begin // SENDING
                    if (ack) begin
                        state <= 0; // Move back to IDLE on ACK
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire clk_ref,            // Reference clock input
    input wire [7:0] frac_value,   // Fractional value input
    output reg clk_out             // Output clock
);
    reg [15:0] counter;            // Counter for frequency division
    reg [15:0] frac_counter;       // Counter for fractional part
    reg [15:0] frac_divider;       // Divider for fractional logic
    reg clk_div;                   // Divided clock

    always @(posedge clk_ref) begin
        counter <= counter + 1;
        if (counter >= (1 << frac_value[4:0])) begin
            clk_div <= ~clk_div;           // Toggle divided clock
            counter <= 0;                  // Reset counter
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk_div) begin
        frac_counter <= frac_counter + 1;
        if (frac_counter >= frac_value) begin
            clk_out <= ~clk_out;            // Generate output clock
            frac_counter <= 0;              // Reset fractional counter
        end
    end
endmodule

Design an Ethernet MAC controller that handles transmission of data frames. The controller should have an input for data, a control signal to indicate whether the data should be sent or not, and an output to indicate that the data has been successfully transmitted. The controller should also maintain a status register that indicates the current state of transmission.
code:
module ethernet_mac_controller (
    input clk,
    input rst_n,
    input [7:0] data_in,
    input send,
    output reg tx_done,
    output reg [7:0] status_reg
);
    reg [1:0] state; // 0: idle, 1: transmitting, 2: done

    always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
        if (!rst_n) begin
            state <= 0;
            tx_done <= 0;
            status_reg <= 8'h00;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin
                    tx_done <= 0;
                    if (send) begin
                        status_reg <= data_in; // Load data into status register
                        state <= 1; // Move to transmitting state
                    end
                end
                1: begin
                    // Simulate transmission delay
                    tx_done <= 0;
                    state <= 2; // Move to done state after transmitting
                end
                2: begin
                    tx_done <= 1; // Transmission done
                    state <= 0; // Go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 4-bit barrel shifter that can perform left and right shifts. The barrel shifter should have a control input to indicate the direction of the shift and a select input to determine how many bits to shift. The design should support shifting by 0 to 3 bits.

module barrel_shifter (
    input [3:0] data_in,
    input [1:0] shift_amount,
    input direction, // 0 for left, 1 for right
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    
    always @(*) begin
        if (direction == 0) begin // left shift
            case (shift_amount)
                2'b00: data_out = data_in;           // no shift
                2'b01: data_out = data_in << 1;      // shift left by 1
                2'b10: data_out = data_in << 2;      // shift left by 2
                2'b11: data_out = data_in << 3;      // shift left by 3
                default: data_out = 4'b0000;         // should never occur
            endcase
        end else begin // right shift
            case (shift_amount)
                2'b00: data_out = data_in;           // no shift
                2'b01: data_out = data_in >> 1;      // shift right by 1
                2'b10: data_out = data_in >> 2;      // shift right by 2
                2'b11: data_out = data_in >> 3;      // shift right by 3
                default: data_out = 4'b0000;         // should never occur
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a 2-channel DMA controller that manages the transfer of data from two different sources to a common destination. The controller should have the following inputs and outputs:
- Inputs:
  - `clk`: Clock signal
  - `reset`: Reset signal
  - `req_a`: Request signal from channel A
  - `req_b`: Request signal from channel B
  - `ack_a`: Acknowledge signal for channel A
  - `ack_b`: Acknowledge signal for channel B
  - `data_in_a`: Data input from channel A
  - `data_in_b`: Data input from channel B
- Outputs:
  - `data_out`: Data output to the destination
  - `active_channel`: Indicates which channel is currently active (0 for A, 1 for B)

The DMA controller should prioritize channel A when both channels request data simultaneously.
code:
module dma_controller (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input req_a,
    input req_b,
    input ack_a,
    input ack_b,
    input [7:0] data_in_a,
    input [7:0] data_in_b,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg active_channel
);
    reg state; // 0 for idle, 1 for transferring

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            active_channel <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Idle state
                    if (req_a) begin
                        active_channel <= 0;
                        data_out <= data_in_a;
                        state <= 1; // Transition to transferring state
                    end else if (req_b) begin
                        active_channel <= 1;
                        data_out <= data_in_b;
                        state <= 1; // Transition to transferring state
                    end
                end
                1: begin // Transferring state
                    if (active_channel == 0 && ack_a) begin
                        state <= 0; // Go back to idle
                    end else if (active_channel == 1 && ack_b) begin
                        state <= 0; // Go back to idle
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple neural network layer with backpropagation. The weights for the inputs will be initialized at the beginning of the simulation and will be updated using a fixed learning rate during backpropagation after each input is processed. The initial weights W1, W2, and W3 should be represented as 4-bit signed integers. The activation function is a simple linear function with no threshold. Implement the weight update rule: W_new = W_old + learning_rate * error * input.

Design a Voltage-Controlled Oscillator (VCO) in Verilog that generates an output frequency based on a control voltage input. The frequency output should vary linearly with the control voltage, and the VCO should have a maximum and minimum frequency limit. Implement a module that includes a control voltage input (4 bits), a clock input, and a frequency output (8 bits).

Design a FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queue with the following specifications:
- The FIFO should have a width of 8 bits and can store up to 4 words.
- It should have inputs for data to be pushed into the queue, a read enable signal, a write enable signal, and a reset signal.
- The outputs should include the data at the front of the queue and an empty flag indicating whether the queue is empty.

Design a 64-bit up-counter in Verilog that counts from 0 to 2^64 - 1. The counter should increment on every positive edge of the clock signal and reset to 0 when a reset signal is asserted. The counter should be enabled by an enable signal. Implement this functionality while ensuring that the counter wraps around correctly after reaching the maximum value.

Design a simple echo cancellation system in Verilog. The system should take an input signal and a reference signal. The echo cancellation should adjust the output based on a simple filter logic that takes the input and reference signals and provides an output that reduces the echo effect. The design should include parameters like the filter coefficients and should be able to process the signals in a clock-driven manner.

Design an interrupt controller that manages multiple interrupt requests (IRQ). The controller should have a single output signal `IRQ_OUT` that is asserted when there is at least one active interrupt request. The input signals are `IRQ0`, `IRQ1`, `IRQ2`, and `IRQ3`, which represent four different interrupt requests. The interrupt requests are active high. Also, there should be a `RESET` signal to clear the state of the interrupt controller.

A 4-channel DMA controller that allows data transfer between memory and peripherals. The controller should have control signals to enable each channel and a clock signal to synchronize the data transfers. Each channel should have a request signal (req), an acknowledge signal (ack), and a data bus (data). When a request is detected on a channel, the DMA controller should grant access to that channel, transfer data, and then release it after acknowledgment.
Design an 8-to-1 multiplexer using Verilog. The multiplexer should have 8 data inputs (d0 to d7), 3 select lines (s2, s1, s0), and 1 output (y).
code:
module mux8to1 (
    input wire [7:0] d, // 8 data inputs
    input wire [2:0] s, // 3 select lines
    output wire y       // output
);
    assign y = d[s]; // output is the selected data input
endmodule

description: Design a combinational logic circuit that implements a simple graph coloring algorithm for a bipartite graph. The circuit should take a binary representation of the edges of the graph and output a coloring of the graph using two colors (0 and 1) such that no two adjacent nodes have the same color. You should assume a maximum of 4 nodes in the graph, represented by a 4x4 adjacency matrix.

Design a dual edge-triggered D flip-flop phase detector. The phase detector should have two inputs, A and B, and an output that indicates whether the phase of input A leads, lags, or is in sync with input B. The output should be 2 bits: 00 for lagging, 01 for leading, and 10 for in sync.
code:
module phase_detector (
    input wire clk,
    input wire A,
    input wire B,
    output reg [1:0] phase_out
);

    reg A_prev, B_prev;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        A_prev <= A;
        B_prev <= B;
        if (A_prev == B_prev) begin
            phase_out <= 2'b10; // In sync
        end else if (A_prev && !B_prev) begin
            phase_out <= 2'b01; // A leads B
        end else begin
            phase_out <= 2'b00; // A lags B
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 24-bit ADC input processing module that scales the input value to a 10-bit output value. The input is a 24-bit unsigned integer, and the output should be the 10-bit representation scaled to the range of 0-1023. The scaling should be done by dividing the input value by 2^14. If the input value exceeds 2^24 - 1, the output should be set to 1023 (the maximum value for a 10-bit number).
Design a clock gating circuit that enables or disables the clock signal to a flip-flop based on an enable signal. The output of the flip-flop should be updated only when the clock is enabled.
code:
module clock_gating(
    input wire clk,
    input wire enable,
    input wire d,
    output reg q
);
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (enable) begin
            q <= d;
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit data bus multiplexer (MUX) that takes four 8-bit input data lines (A, B, C, D) and selects one of them based on a 2-bit select line (S). The output should be the selected 8-bit data line.

Design a 16-bit shift register that can shift left or right based on a control signal. The shift register should have a parallel load feature, allowing it to load a 16-bit value when a load signal is asserted. The control signal determines the shifting direction: '0' for left shift and '1' for right shift. The shift register's output should be available at its output port.
code:
module shift_register (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input load,
    input [15:0] parallel_in,
    input shift_dir,  // 0 for left, 1 for right
    output reg [15:0] q
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            q <= 16'b0;  // Clear the register on reset
        end else if (load) begin
            q <= parallel_in;  // Load parallel input
        end else if (shift_dir == 1'b0) begin
            q <= {q[14:0], 1'b0};  // Shift left
        end else begin
            q <= {1'b0, q[15:1]};  // Shift right
        end
    end
endmodule

description: A 4-bit SRAM cell that allows writing and reading of 4-bit data. The memory cell should have control signals for read and write operations. The design should handle read and write enable signals, and the data should be stored and retrieved correctly based on these controls.
code:
module SRAM4Bit (
    input wire clk,
    input wire write_enable,
    input wire read_enable,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    output reg [3:0] data_out
);
    reg [3:0] memory;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (write_enable) begin
            memory <= data_in; // Write data to memory
        end
    end
    
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (read_enable) begin
            data_out <= memory; // Read data from memory
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a simple DES-like encryption module that takes an 8-bit plaintext and a 8-bit key, and produces an 8-bit ciphertext. The encryption process consists of a simple XOR operation with the key and a left rotation operation. The output will be the result of the encryption process.

Design a Turbo Encoder that takes a 4-bit input data and encodes it using two convolutional encoders in parallel, followed by an interleaver. The output should be a 12-bit encoded data consisting of the outputs of both encoders and the interleaved data.

Design a Fixed-Priority Arbiter in Verilog that selects one of four requests (req[3:0]) based on a fixed priority scheme. The arbiter should output a grant signal (grant) indicating which request is granted. The priority is fixed as follows: req[0] has the highest priority, followed by req[1], req[2], and req[3] having the lowest priority. If multiple requests are active, the highest priority request should be granted.
code:
module fixed_priority_arbiter(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [3:0] req,
    output reg [3:0] grant
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        grant <= 4'b0000;
    end else begin
        grant <= 4'b0000; // Reset grant
        if (req[0]) grant <= 4'b0001; // Grant req[0]
        else if (req[1]) grant <= 4'b0010; // Grant req[1]
        else if (req[2]) grant <= 4'b0100; // Grant req[2]
        else if (req[3]) grant <= 4'b1000; // Grant req[3]
    end
end

endmodule

description: A 1-bit DRAM cell that can be written to and read from. The DRAM cell has a data input, a write enable signal, a read enable signal, and outputs the stored data. The cell should retain the data until a write operation occurs.
code:
module dram_cell (

    input wire read_en,  
    input wire data_in,  
    output reg data_out  
);

        end  
    end

        end

description: Design a 32-bit up counter that counts from 0 to 2^32-1. The counter should have a clock input, a reset input, and a enable input. When reset is high, the counter should reset to 0. When enable is high, the counter should increment on each rising edge of the clock.
code:
module counter_32bit (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire en,
    output reg [31:0] count
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        count <= 32'b0;
    end else if (en) begin
        count <= count + 1;
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a 2D support vector machine (SVM) decision function in Verilog, which takes two 8-bit inputs representing features x and y, and outputs a 1-bit result indicating the class (0 or 1) based on a linear decision boundary. The decision function can be represented as `w0*x + w1*y + b > 0`. Use weights `w0 = 3`, `w1 = 2`, and bias `b = -5`.

Design a voltage sensor system in Verilog that monitors a voltage input signal and triggers an alert if the voltage exceeds a predefined threshold. The sensor should have a clock input and must be able to reset. It should output a high signal if the threshold is exceeded, and a low signal otherwise. The state of the output should be updated on the rising edge of the clock.
code:
module voltage_sensor (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] voltage_input,
    input wire [7:0] threshold,
    output reg alert
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        alert <= 0;
    end else begin
        if (voltage_input > threshold) begin
            alert <= 1;
        end else begin
            alert <= 0;
        end
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a T-latch in Verilog that toggles its output state based on an input signal T (toggle). The latch should have an asynchronous reset signal R, which, when activated, sets the output Q to 0 regardless of the state of T. The output Q should hold its value when R is not activated and T is inactive.
code:
module T_latch (
    input wire T,
    input wire R,
    output reg Q
);
    always @(posedge T or posedge R) begin
        if (R) begin
            Q <= 0; // Asynchronous reset
        end else begin
            Q <= ~Q; // Toggle operation
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 4th-order IIR filter using Verilog that takes a 16-bit input sample and produces a 16-bit output sample. The filter coefficients should be predefined in the module and the filter should operate on a clock with a reset signal. The filter should maintain internal state across clock cycles to implement the feedback required for the IIR filter.
Design an Adaptive LMS filter that adjusts its coefficients based on the input signal to minimize the error between the desired signal and the output signal.

Design a simple Flash memory cell in Verilog. The Flash memory cell should have a single input `data_in`, a control signal `write_enable`, and a single output `data_out`. When `write_enable` is high, the `data_in` should be stored and appear at `data_out`. When `write_enable` is low, `data_out` should hold the last value written.
code:
module flash_memory (
    input wire data_in,
    input wire write_enable,
    output reg data_out
);
    always @(*) begin
        if (write_enable) begin
            data_out = data_in; // Store the input value
        end
        // If not writing, retain the last value
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit DRAM cell with a write and read operation. The cell should have inputs for data (8 bits), a write enable signal, and an output for the stored data (8 bits). When the write enable signal is high, the data should be written to the cell. When the write enable signal is low, the output should reflect the stored data.

        end

    end

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a simple singly linked list traversal. The module should allow for inserting new nodes at the end of the list, and it should also provide a mechanism to traverse the list and output the values of the nodes in the order they were added. The linked list should be able to hold a predefined number of elements, say 5, and it should not allow for overflow by adding more than this number. The module should have the following inputs and outputs: inputs for the data to insert and a clock signal; outputs for the current node data and a valid signal to indicate whether the output is valid.

Design a 4-bit divider circuit that divides a 4-bit dividend by a 4-bit divisor, producing a 4-bit quotient and a 4-bit remainder. The circuit should operate synchronously with a clock, and the output should be valid after a division operation is completed.

Design a Verilog module that computes the checksum of an 8-bit input data. The checksum is computed by summing the 8-bit input data and taking the lower 4 bits of the sum as the checksum. The module should have an input for the 8-bit data and an output for the 4-bit checksum.

Implement a 4-bit Quick Sort module that sorts an array of 4 4-bit inputs. The module should be capable of sorting the input values in ascending order. You may assume that the inputs will be provided in a register and the sorted output should also be available in a register after a clock cycle. The sorting should be done in a single clock cycle, and the inputs and outputs must be correctly synchronized.

Design a Reed-Solomon encoder module in Verilog that takes a message of 8 bits and generates a codeword of 15 bits. The encoder should implement a simple Reed-Solomon encoding scheme with predefined parameters suitable for the input size. The module should include a state machine to manage the encoding process and should be capable of handling various input messages sequentially.

Design a simple UART transmitter that takes an 8-bit data input, a start bit, and a stop bit. The transmitter should output the bits in the correct order: start bit, data bits (from LSB to MSB), and stop bit. The transmitter should operate on a clock edge and include a state machine to manage the transmission process.

Design a 1-bit DRAM cell that has the following characteristics:  
- It has a data input (D), a control signal (WE for Write Enable), and a data output (Q).  
- When WE is high, the data input D should be written to the cell, and when WE is low, the cell should hold the stored value, which is output on Q.  
- The cell should also respond to a reset signal (RST), which, when high, sets Q to 0 regardless of WE.
code:
module dram_cell (
    input wire D,         // Data input
    input wire WE,       // Write Enable
    input wire RST,      // Reset
    output reg Q         // Data output
);
    always @ (posedge WE or posedge RST) begin
        if (RST) begin
            Q <= 1'b0;    // Reset Q to 0
        end else begin
            Q <= D;       // Write D to Q
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a 16-bit DRAM cell that can store and retrieve data. The DRAM cell should have the following functionality:
- A 16-bit input data bus (data_in) for writing data to the cell.
- A 16-bit output data bus (data_out) for reading data from the cell.
- A write enable signal (we) that, when high, allows data to be written to the cell.
- A read enable signal (re) that, when high, allows data to be read from the cell.
The data should be held until a new write is initiated, and reading should provide the recently written data.

Design a simple position encoder for a robot which increments its position based on direction input (forward or backward). The robot has a 4-bit position register. When the direction input is '1', the position increments by 1; when the direction input is '0', the position decrements by 1. The position wraps around when it exceeds its maximum value (15) or goes below 0.
code:
module position_encoder (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input direction, // 1 for forward, 0 for backward
    output reg [3:0] position
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset)
            position <= 4'b0000; // reset position to 0
        else begin
            if (direction) begin
                position <= (position == 4'b1111) ? 4'b0000 : position + 1'b1; // wrap around
            end else begin
                position <= (position == 4'b0000) ? 4'b1111 : position - 1'b1; // wrap around
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a power gating circuit with two inputs (A, B) and one output (Y). The output Y should be high (1) only when both A and B are high (1). When either A or B is low (0), Y should be low (0). Additionally, implement a power gating control signal P, where the output Y should only be active (reflect the values of A and B) when P is high (1). If P is low (0), the output Y should be low (0) regardless of A and B. This behavior represents a simple power gating mechanism.
Design a combinational circuit to evaluate the polynomial P(x) = 3x^3 + 2x^2 + 1 for a given 4-bit input x (0 to 15). The output should be a 10-bit result.
code:
module polynomial_evaluator (
    input [3:0] x,
    output reg [9:0] P
);
    always @(*) begin
        P = 3 * (x * x * x) + 2 * (x * x) + 1; // Evaluate the polynomial
    end
endmodule

description: Design a SHA-256 hash function module that takes a 512-bit message input and outputs a 256-bit hash value. The module should include the initialization of hash values and the application of the SHA-256 processing steps (message padding, message schedule, compression function). The full functionality of SHA-256 is not required; you need to implement just the main structure and key operations, which can be expanded later.

Design a Verilog module that implements a simple gradient descent optimization algorithm. The module takes a data point (x) and its corresponding gradient (d) as inputs, along with a learning rate (lr). It updates the parameter (theta) based on the gradient and learning rate. The output is the updated value of theta after the adjustment.
code:
module gradient_descent (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input [15:0] x,
    input [15:0] d,
    input [15:0] lr,
    output reg [15:0] theta
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            theta <= 16'h0000; // Initialize theta to 0
        end else begin
            theta <= theta - (lr * d); // Update theta
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit deserializer that takes a single input bit stream and deserializes it into 8 output bits. The input is provided at a clock edge, and the output is ready after 8 clock cycles. The output should be valid only when the `valid` signal is high.
code:
module deserializer (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input din,
    input valid,
    output reg [7:0] dout
);
    reg [2:0] bit_count; // 3 bits to count up to 8

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            dout <= 8'b0;
            bit_count <= 3'b0;
        end else if (valid) begin
            dout <= {dout[6:0], din}; // Shift in the new bit
            if (bit_count < 3'd7)
                bit_count <= bit_count + 3'd1;
            else
                bit_count <= 3'b0; // Reset after 8 bits
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Create a 2-channel DMA controller that can transfer data from a source address to a destination address. The DMA controller should have the following inputs: a clock signal (clk), a reset signal (rst), a start signal (start), two source addresses (src_addr0, src_addr1), two destination addresses (dest_addr0, dest_addr1), and an enable signal for each channel (enable0, enable1). The DMA controller should output a done signal (done) indicating when the transfer is complete. The controller should switch between the two channels based on the start signal and whether each channel is enabled.

Design a 32-bit serializer that takes a 32-bit parallel input and converts it into a serial output. The serializer should shift out one bit per clock cycle. Include an enable signal that starts the serialization process. The output should be valid only when the enable signal is high. The serializer should also have a reset signal that initializes the output and state.
code:
module serializer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire enable,
    input wire [31:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [4:0] bit_counter; // 5 bits to count from 0 to 31

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            bit_counter <= 5'b0;
            serial_out <= 1'b0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            if (bit_counter < 32) begin
                serial_out <= parallel_in[31 - bit_counter]; // Shift out MSB first
                bit_counter <= bit_counter + 1;
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module that implements a simplified version of the SHA-256 hash function. The module should take a 512-bit input message and produce a 256-bit hash output. Include an internal state to maintain the current hash value, and use a clock and reset signal to control the processing. The design should include state transitions to process the input message in chunks, and the final hash should be output after processing.

Design a 32-bit up/down counter in Verilog. The counter should increment when the `up` signal is high and decrement when the `down` signal is high. The counter should also have a synchronous reset signal to reset the counter to zero.
code:
module counter_32bit (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input up,
    input down,
    output reg [31:0] count
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        count <= 32'b0;
    end else if (up && !down) begin
        count <= count + 1;
    end else if (down && !up) begin
        count <= count - 1;
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design an 8-channel DMA controller that can transfer data from a source to a destination based on a control signal. The controller should have an enable signal and a reset signal, and it should also provide an output indicating which channel is currently active.

Design an Up/Down counter in Verilog that counts up when a control signal (`up`) is high and counts down when it is low. The counter should reset to zero when a reset signal (`reset`) is high. The counter should be 4 bits wide and should have a maximum count of 15. If the counter exceeds 15 while counting up, it should wrap around to 0. If it goes below 0 while counting down, it should also wrap around to 15.
code:
module UpDownCounter (
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input up,
    output reg [3:0] count
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            count <= 4'b0000; // Reset the counter to 0
        end else if (up) begin
            count <= (count == 4'b1111) ? 4'b0000 : count + 1; // Count up with wrap-around
        end else begin
            count <= (count == 4'b0000) ? 4'b1111 : count - 1; // Count down with wrap-around
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design a LIFO stack module in Verilog. The stack should support the following operations:
1. Push: Insert an item onto the stack.
2. Pop: Remove the item from the top of the stack.
3. Peek: Retrieve the item from the top of the stack without removing it.
4. IsEmpty: Check if the stack is empty.

The stack should have a defined size (e.g., 8 items) and you should include control signals for push and pop operations, along with the data input and output signals.

Design a Verilog module that implements a basic SD card command response handler. The module should accept a command signal (`cmd`) and a clock signal (`clk`). When a command is received, the module generates a response signal (`resp`) based on the command type. The response should be generated in two clock cycles: the first cycle should assert a 'busy' indication, and the second cycle should provide the actual response. The commands can be simple integers (0 to 3) representing different operations. Make sure to handle commands 0 to 3 with respective responses, e.g., command 0 returns response 0x01, command 1 returns response 0x02, etc.

Design a Verilog module that implements a simple HMAC operation. The module should take a key and a message as inputs and produce an HMAC output using a simple hash function (like XOR for simplicity). The key and message lengths should be fixed at 8 bits each, and the output should be 8 bits as well.
code:
module hmac_simple (  
    input [7:0] key,  
    input [7:0] message,  
    output [7:0] hmac  
);

endmodule

description: Design a 16-bit DRAM cell with read and write capabilities. The DRAM cell should have an input data signal (16 bits wide), a control signal for write (1 bit), a read control signal (1 bit), and an output data signal (16 bits wide). When the write control signal is high, the input data should be stored in the cell. When the read control signal is high, the stored data should be outputted.

    input wire [15:0] data_in,
    input wire write_en,
    input wire read_en,
    output reg [15:0] data_out
);
    reg [15:0] memory;

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (write_en) begin
            memory <= data_in; // Store input data in memory
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (read_en) begin
            data_out <= memory; // Output stored data
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design an 8-bit SRAM memory cell that can read and write data. The SRAM cell should have inputs for a write enable signal (we), an 8-bit data input (data_in), an 8-bit data output (data_out), and a clock signal (clk). The memory should store the data when the write enable signal is high and the clock has a rising edge. When the write enable is low, the output should always reflect the stored data.

module SRAM_Cell (

    input wire [7:0] data_in,

);

        end

    end

description: Design a 5-to-32 decoder in Verilog. The decoder takes a 5-bit input and activates one of the 32 output lines based on the input value. For example, if the input is 3'b00000, the output line 0 should be activated (set to 1), and all other output lines should be deactivated (set to 0).
code:
module decoder_5_to_32 (

    output reg [31:0] out
);

        out = 32'b0; // Default all outputs to 0
        out[in] = 1'b1; // Activate the output corresponding to the input
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Verilog module for a phase-locked loop (PLL) that can recover a carrier frequency from a modulated input signal. The PLL should consist of a phase detector, low-pass filter, and voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO). The input signal will be a binary modulated signal, and the output should be a recovered clock signal. The module must handle the synchronization process to ensure that the output clock is in phase with the input signal.
Design a Verilog module that performs matrix multiplication for two 2x2 matrices. The input will be two 2x2 matrices, and the output will be the resulting 2x2 matrix.
code:

description:

1. A sender module that transmits data and waits for an acknowledgment (ACK) from the receiver.
2. A receiver module that checks the received data for errors and sends back an ACK or NACK (Negative Acknowledgment) based on the validity of the data.
3. The system should be able to retry sending the data if a NACK is received.
4. Implement a simple parity check for the error detection.
5. The sender should have a maximum of 3 retries before giving up.

The sender and receiver should communicate through a simple handshake mechanism.
code:
module arq_system (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    input wire ack,
    output reg [7:0] data_out,
    output reg send,
    output reg retry
);
    reg [2:0] state;
    reg [2:0] retry_count;
    parameter IDLE = 3'b000, SEND = 3'b001, WAIT_ACK = 3'b010, RETRY = 3'b011, DONE = 3'b100;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            retry_count <= 0;
            send <= 0;
            retry <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    data_out <= data_in; // Prepare data to send
                    state <= SEND;
                end
                
                SEND: begin
                    send <= 1; // Indicate sending data
                    state <= WAIT_ACK;
                end
                
                WAIT_ACK: begin
                    if (ack) begin
                        send <= 0; // Acknowledged
                        state <= DONE;
                    end else begin
                        if (retry_count < 3) begin
                            retry_count <= retry_count + 1;
                            state <= RETRY;
                        end else begin
                            state <= DONE; // Give up after retries
                        end
                    end
                end
                
                RETRY: begin
                    send <= 1; // Retry sending data
                    state <= WAIT_ACK;
                end
                
                DONE: begin
                    send <= 0;
                    retry <= 0; // Finish operation
                    state <= IDLE; // Reset state to IDLE
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

            if (remainder[4]) begin // If remainder is negative

- 1010: SLL (Shift Left Logical)
- 1011: SRL (Shift Right Logical)

    output reg [31:0] result,
    output reg Z
);

        case (opcode)
            4'b0000: result = A & B;         // AND
            4'b0001: result = A | B;         // OR
            4'b0010: result = A ^ B;         // XOR
            4'b0011: result = A + B;         // ADD
            4'b0100: result = A - B;         // SUB

            4'b1101: result = A;              // PASS A
            4'b1110: result = B;              // PASS B
            4'b1111: result = 32'b0;          // NOP
            default: result = 32'b0;          // Default case

                2'b01: if (branch_taken) state <= 2'b10;  // Weakly Taken
                        else state <= 2'b00;  // Strongly Not Taken
                2'b10: if (branch_taken) state <= 2'b11;  // Strongly Taken

    reg [4:0] D; // Current value of dividend

    input wire ack,
    output reg [3:0] int_out,
    output reg int_active
);

            active_interrupts <= active_interrupts & ~int_out; // Clear acknowledged interrupt

        int_active = |active_interrupts; // Set active flag if any interrupt is active

endmodule

module piso_shift_register (
    input wire clk,
    input wire load,
    input wire [4:0] parallel_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [4:0] shift_reg;
    integer count;

            shift_reg <= parallel_in; // Load data into the shift register

    end
endmodule
